```markdown
CSS (use verbatim):

~~~css
/* Hero portrait with magnet */
.hero-portrait-wrap {
  position: absolute;
  left: 50%;
  transform: translateX(-50%);
  z-index: 10;
  width: 400px;
  top: 50%;
  transform: translate(-50%, -50%);
  touch-action: pan-y;
}
.hero-portrait-inner {
  transition: transform 0.6s ease-in-out;
  will-change: transform;
}
.hero-portrait-inner { position: relative; }
.hero-portrait-inner img {
  display: block;
  width: 100%;
  height: auto;
  object-fit: contain;
  user-select: none;
  -webkit-user-drag: none;
}
#faceGl { position: absolute; left: -35%; top: -35%; width: 170%; height: 170%; pointer-events: none; }
#faceProps { position: absolute; inset: 0; pointer-events: none; }
#faceFly, #faceHand { position: absolute; opacity: 0; transition: opacity .2s; transform: translate(-50%, -50%); }
#faceFly { width: 6%; fill: #111; }
#faceFly .wing { fill: rgba(220, 235, 255, .7); transform-origin: 16px 15px; animation: flap .05s linear infinite alternate; }
#faceFly .wing.r { animation-direction: alternate-reverse; }
@keyframes flap { from { transform: rotate(-16deg); } to { transform: rotate(16deg); } }
#faceHand { width: 11%; fill: #fff; stroke: #0c0c0c; stroke-width: 1.4; stroke-linejoin: round; }
#faceHand .grab { display: none; }
#faceHand.shut .open { display: none; }
#faceHand.shut .grab { display: block; }
~~~
```

- **Poster 1280px:** https://images.higgs.ai/?default=1&output=webp&url=https%3A%2F%2Fd8j0ntlcm91z4.cloudfront.net%2Fuser_38xzZboKViGWJOttwIXH07lWA1P%2Fhf_20261101_054911_1a9c58cf-98a9-48a6-b438-bd78b9e58839.png&w=1280&q=85

```markdown
# Video Ribbon — Vante Scroll Portfolio Hero (exact recreation prompt)

Build a single-file, full-viewport, scroll-driven portfolio hero called **Vante**. On a near-black page, the two-part headline `CRAFT IN` / `MOTION` slides across the screen in opposite directions while a continuous ribbon of live video cards spirals around the viewer in 3D. It starts small along the bottom, swings close in a shallow curved arc, wraps around the left edge, runs away along the top and leaves top right. Then the cards land one by one in a calm 3×2 grid.

Plain HTML, CSS and one vanilla ES module in one file. The only external resources are the Google Fonts, three.js 0.170.0 from jsDelivr and the eight video URLs listed below. Reproduce every value, string and timing exactly. The CSS, markup and script are given verbatim, so copy them without changes.

Four rules define it:
1. **Everything comes from one number.** Scroll progress `p` from 0 to 1, smoothed with `p += (target - p) * .09` each frame, drives everything. Scrolling back reverses it perfectly.
2. **The ribbon runs on a fixed rail.** The path never moves. The ribbon only slides along it, card after card.
3. **Text always reads correctly.** The cards are a two-sided strip. When a card is seen from behind on the near pass, the fragment shader flips `uv.x`, so videos are never mirrored.
4. **The curve stays gentle up close.** The near pass is a shallow arc, about 5.4 to 7.6 units from the camera, so the middle card stays wide and flat. The far runs reach 24 units away, so the cards look tiny there.

---

## 1. Page basics

- Title: `Vante — Craft in Motion`
- Meta description: `A studio portfolio where a ribbon of live video work sweeps through space, then lands in a grid.`
- Fonts: `https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=IBM+Plex+Mono:wght@400;500&family=Inter+Tight:wght@400;500;600&display=swap`, with preconnects to fonts.googleapis.com and fonts.gstatic.com (crossorigin).
- Import map: `three` → `https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.170.0/build/three.module.js`
- Colours: background `#0a0a0b`, ink `#f4f1ea`, mid `#8d8b86`, line `rgba(244,241,234,.14)`.
- Structure: `#track` is 900vh tall and holds a sticky 100vh `.stage`.

## 2. Videos (use these exact URLs)

All are hosted with `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *` and are loaded with `crossOrigin="anonymous"`, muted, looping and inline. Each one is a `THREE.VideoTexture`.

1. Roadster 3D: `https://pub-86dc5b5484314368ac5436a674b0d919.r2.dev/designs/roadster-3d-car-landing.mp4`
2. Living Portrait: `https://pub-86dc5b5484314368ac5436a674b0d919.r2.dev/aaaf/living-portrait-hero.mp4`
3. Particle Self: `https://pub-86dc5b5484314368ac5436a674b0d919.r2.dev/aaaf/oraciteslArea.mp4`
4. Robot Jellyfish: `https://pub-86dc5b5484314368ac5436a674b0d919.r2.dev/aaaf/medusa-jellyfish-hero.mp4`
5. Ink Reveal: `https://pub-86dc5b5484314368ac5436a674b0d919.r2.dev/designs/ink-reveal-hover.mp4`
6. Space Voyage: `https://pub-86dc5b5484314368ac5436a674b0d919.r2.dev/designs/space-voyage-video.mp4`
7. Helion Dispatch: `https://pub-86dc5b5484314368ac5436a674b0d919.r2.dev/designs/helion-dispatch-landing.mp4`
8. Honey Bee: `https://pub-86dc5b5484314368ac5436a674b0d919.r2.dev/designs/honey-bee-melli-landing.mp4`

The first six land in the grid. The last two appear only in the ribbon. Videos play only while their card is visible.

## 3. Layout

- **Top left:** a small triangular mark and `VANTE`, then two boxed pager arrows `←` and `→` hanging from the top edge.
- **Top centre:** `START A PROJECT →` in IBM Plex Mono with an underline.
- **Top right:** a `LET'S TALK` pill with a dot and a `MENU` pill with a two-line icon.
- **Bottom left:** `Concepts, explorations and interface experiments shared openly as part of our creative process.`
- **Bottom centre:** `VISUALS / FILM / MUSIC / EXPERIMENTS`. **Bottom right:** `VIEW SHOWREEL` with a short line.
- **Centre:** the caption `Exploring ideas through daily design practice.`, small and uppercase, between the two headline lines.
- **Headline:** Inter Tight 400, `clamp(40px,6.7vw,130px)`, letter-spacing `-.055em`. The two lines are offset horizontally and stack about one line apart.

## 4. First frame

At `p = 0` the screen looks almost empty and technical. A soft lighter glow fades down from the top over 42% of the height. A hairline with a small `+` at its centre crosses at 37.5% of the height. Only the end of the headline shows: `IN` at the far left edge and the start of `M` at the far right edge, both low on the screen, with the caption low in the centre. The glow, hairline, pager and `START A PROJECT` link fade out by `p = .05`.

## 5. Scroll timeline

| Progress | What happens |
|---|---|
| 0–.12 | Headline and caption rise 34vh into place |
| 0–.58 | `CRAFT IN` runs from -50vw to +76vw, `MOTION` runs the opposite way, crossing near .24 |
| .14–.63 | Ribbon slides along the whole rail |
| .52–.57 | Caption fades |
| As each card leaves the rail | That card flies straight to its grid slot over .13 of scroll, so there is never an empty screen |
| .72–.86 | A hairline draws across between the two rows |

A card is on the rail until it reaches the end of it, then it switches to its grid pose. Each card flies in from its own side with a small tilt, eased with `1-(1-t)^3`. Top row cards come from above, bottom row cards from below, outer cards from the sides.

## 6. The ribbon rail

Built from 161 sampled points as a centripetal `CatmullRomCurve3`, read back by arc length into a table of 1201 points and tangents. For `t` in 0–1 and `ph` from `-1.5` to `2π + 1.35`:

- `cs = cos(ph)`
- `depth = cs > 0 ? 7.6 + 16.4 * cs^.9 : 7.6 + 2.2 * cs`
- `edge = .84 + .5 * span(.14 - t, 0, .14) + .8 * span(t, .84, 1)`
- `u = 2t - 1`
- Point: `(edge * sin(ph) * depth * .561, .5 * sign(u) * |u|^1.4 * depth * .63, -depth)`

Cards are 2.1 × 1.32 units with a gap of .03, so they read as one strip. Each is a `PlaneGeometry` with 28 × 3 segments whose vertices are rewritten every frame by walking the rail. The local up vector is world Y made perpendicular to the tangent.

Camera: field of view 35°. Below 16:9 the field of view is recalculated with `atan(.561 / aspect)` so the horizontal view stays fixed and the ribbon is never squashed on a narrower window.

## 7. Card shader

A `ShaderMaterial` with an analytic rounded rectangle (`radius .018`), a cover fit from the video's aspect ratio, a dark placeholder of `vec3(.075)` until the video loads, a faint light edge, and `if(!gl_FrontFacing) uv.x = 1. - uv.x`. Output colour space is linear passthrough, with texture colour space `NoColorSpace`, so the videos keep their true colours.

## 8. Grid

Three columns and two rows on a plane at z = -8, 74% of the view width, gap 1.7% of that width. Below an aspect of .9 it becomes two columns and three rows at 88% width. Past `p = .86`, hovering a card shows a small ink pill with the design name that follows the cursor.

## 11. Script (use verbatim, as `<script type="module">`)

~~~js
import * as THREE from 'three';

const R2 = 'https://pub-86dc5b5484314368ac5436a674b0d919.r2.dev/';
const WORK = [
  ['Roadster 3D', 'designs/roadster-3d-car-landing.mp4'],
  ['Living Portrait', 'aaaf/living-portrait-hero.mp4'],
  ['Particle Self', 'aaaf/oraciteslArea.mp4'],
  ['Robot Jellyfish', 'aaaf/medusa-jellyfish-hero.mp4'],
  ['Ink Reveal', 'designs/ink-reveal-hover.mp4'],
  ['Space Voyage', 'designs/space-voyage-video.mp4'],
  ['Helion Dispatch', 'designs/helion-dispatch-landing.mp4'],
  ['Honey Bee', 'designs/honey-bee-melli-landing.mp4'],
];
const $ = id => document.getElementById(id);
const clamp = (x, a = 0, b = 1) => Math.min(b, Math.max(a, x));
const mix = (a, b, t) => a + (b - a) * t;
const ease = t => t * t * (3 - 2 * t);
const out = t => 1 - (1 - t) ** 3;
const span = (p, a, b) => clamp((p - a) / (b - a));

/* ---------- renderer ---------- */
const canvas = $('gl');
const renderer = new THREE.WebGLRenderer({canvas, antialias:true, alpha:true});
renderer.setClearColor(0, 0);
renderer.outputColorSpace = THREE.LinearSRGBColorSpace;
const scene = new THREE.Scene();
const FOV = 35, camera = new THREE.PerspectiveCamera(FOV, 1, .1, 100);

/* ---------- ribbon path ---------- */
let path, PATH_L = 1;
const SAMPLES = 1200, pathP = [], pathT = [];
const PH0 = -1.5, PH1 = Math.PI * 2 + 1.35;
function buildPath() {
  const pts = [];
  for (let i = 0; i <= 160; i++) {
    const t = i / 160, ph = mix(PH0, PH1, t), cs = Math.cos(ph), u = 2 * t - 1;
    // a shallow arc close to the camera, then long runs far behind it
    const depth = cs > 0 ? 7.6 + 16.4 * cs ** .9 : 7.6 + 2.2 * cs;
    const edge = .84 + .5 * span(.14 - t, 0, .14) + .8 * span(t, .84, 1);
    pts.push(new THREE.Vector3(edge * Math.sin(ph) * depth * .561, .5 * Math.sign(u) * Math.abs(u) ** 1.4 * depth * .63, -depth));
  }
  path = new THREE.CatmullRomCurve3(pts, false, 'centripetal');
  path.arcLengthDivisions = 1500;
  PATH_L = path.getLength(); pathP.length = pathT.length = 0;
  for (let i = 0; i <= SAMPLES; i++) { const u = i / SAMPLES; pathP.push(path.getPointAt(u)); pathT.push(path.getTangentAt(u)); }
}
const at = (s, op, ot) => {
  const f = clamp(s / PATH_L) * SAMPLES, i = Math.min(SAMPLES - 1, Math.floor(f)), k = f - i;
  op.lerpVectors(pathP[i], pathP[i + 1], k); ot.lerpVectors(pathT[i], pathT[i + 1], k).normalize();
};

/* ---------- cards ---------- */
const CARD_W = 2.1, CARD_H = 1.32, GAP = .03, STEP = CARD_W + GAP, NX = 28, NY = 3;
const vs = `varying vec2 vUv;void main(){vUv=uv;gl_Position=projectionMatrix*modelViewMatrix*vec4(position,1.);}`;
const fs = `uniform sampler2D map;uniform vec2 cover;uniform float aspect,ready,radius;varying vec2 vUv;
void main(){
  vec2 q=(abs(vUv-.5)-.5)*vec2(aspect,1.)+radius;
  float d=length(max(q,0.))+min(max(q.x,q.y),0.)-radius;
  float px=fwidth(d),a=1.-smoothstep(-px,px,d);
  if(a<.01)discard;
  vec2 uv=vUv;if(!gl_FrontFacing)uv.x=1.-uv.x;
  vec3 c=mix(vec3(.075),texture2D(map,(uv-.5)*cover+.5).rgb,ready);
  float edge=smoothstep(-.012-px,-.012,d);
  gl_FragColor=vec4(mix(c,vec3(1.),edge*.1),a);
}`;
const cards = WORK.map(([title, src], i) => {
  const v = document.createElement('video');
  Object.assign(v, {crossOrigin:'anonymous', muted:true, loop:true, playsInline:true, preload:'auto', src:R2 + src});
  v.setAttribute('playsinline', '');
  const tex = new THREE.VideoTexture(v);
  tex.colorSpace = THREE.NoColorSpace; tex.minFilter = THREE.LinearFilter; tex.magFilter = THREE.LinearFilter; tex.generateMipmaps = false;
  const geo = new THREE.PlaneGeometry(1, 1, NX, NY);
  const mat = new THREE.ShaderMaterial({vertexShader:vs, fragmentShader:fs, transparent:true, side:THREE.DoubleSide,
    uniforms:{map:{value:tex}, cover:{value:new THREE.Vector2(1, 1)}, aspect:{value:CARD_W / CARD_H}, ready:{value:0}, radius:{value:.018}}});
  const mesh = new THREE.Mesh(geo, mat); mesh.frustumCulled = false; scene.add(mesh);
  const c = {i, title, v, tex, geo, mat, mesh, rect:null};
  v.addEventListener('loadeddata', () => {
    const va = v.videoWidth / v.videoHeight, ca = CARD_W / CARD_H;
    mat.uniforms.cover.value.set(va > ca ? ca / va : 1, va > ca ? 1 : va / ca);
    mat.uniforms.ready.value = 1;
  });
  return c;
});

/* ---------- layout ---------- */
const GZ = 8;
let W = 1, H = 1, asp = 1, cols = 3, rows = 2, tanH = .3153;
function resize() {
  W = innerWidth; H = innerHeight; asp = W / H;
  renderer.setPixelRatio(Math.min(devicePixelRatio, 2)); renderer.setSize(W, H, false);
  camera.aspect = asp; camera.fov = asp < 16 / 9 ? Math.atan(.561 / asp) * 360 / Math.PI : FOV; camera.updateProjectionMatrix();
  tanH = Math.tan(camera.fov * Math.PI / 360);
  cols = asp < .9 ? 2 : 3; rows = asp < .9 ? 3 : 2;
  }
addEventListener('resize', resize); resize(); buildPath();
function grid(i) {
  const vh = 2 * GZ * tanH, vw = vh * asp, gw = vw * (cols === 3 ? .74 : .88), gap = gw * .017;
  const cw = (gw - gap * (cols - 1)) / cols, ch = cw / (CARD_W / CARD_H), gh = ch * rows + gap * 1.6 * (rows - 1);
  const c = i % cols, r = Math.floor(i / cols);
  return {x:-gw / 2 + cw / 2 + c * (cw + gap), y:gh / 2 - ch / 2 - r * (ch + gap * 1.6), w:cw, h:ch, vw, vh, c, r};
}

/* ---------- scroll ---------- */
let target = 0, p = 0, frozen = false;
const readScroll = () => { const t = $('track'); target = clamp(scrollY / (t.offsetHeight - innerHeight)); };
addEventListener('scroll', readScroll, {passive:true}); readScroll();

/* ---------- pose ---------- */
const op = new THREE.Vector3(), ot = new THREE.Vector3(), up = new THREE.Vector3(), Y = new THREE.Vector3(0, 1, 0), vp = new THREE.Vector3();
function poseRibbon(c, head) {
  const pos = c.geo.attributes.position, centre = head - c.i * STEP;
  for (let iy = 0; iy <= NY; iy++) for (let ix = 0; ix <= NX; ix++) {
    const k = iy * (NX + 1) + ix, lu = ix / NX - .5, lv = .5 - iy / NY;
    at(centre + lu * CARD_W, op, ot);
    // keep the sheet upright, leaning a little into the turn
        up.copy(Y).addScaledVector(ot, -Y.dot(ot)).normalize();
    vp.copy(op).addScaledVector(up, lv * CARD_H);
    pos.setXYZ(k, vp.x, vp.y, vp.z);
  }
  pos.needsUpdate = true;
}
function poseGrid(c, q) {
  const g = grid(c.i), pos = c.geo.attributes.position;
  const dx = (g.c - (cols - 1) / 2) * 1.2 + (cols === 3 && g.c === 1 ? 0 : 0), dy = g.r < rows / 2 ? 1 : -1;
  const ox = dx * g.vw * .62 * (1 - q), oy = dy * g.vh * (g.c === 1 ? .95 : .34) * (1 - q), tilt = (1 - q) * .22 * (g.c - 1 || .5) * dy;
  const cs = Math.cos(tilt), sn = Math.sin(tilt);
  for (let iy = 0; iy <= NY; iy++) for (let ix = 0; ix <= NX; ix++) {
    const k = iy * (NX + 1) + ix, x = (ix / NX - .5) * g.w, y = (.5 - iy / NY) * g.h;
    pos.setXYZ(k, g.x + ox + x * cs - y * sn, g.y + oy + x * sn + y * cs, -GZ - (1 - q) * .6 * Math.sin(ix / NX * Math.PI));
  }
  pos.needsUpdate = true;
  c.rect = g;
}

const RIB_A = .14, RIB_B = .63;
function setVideos(fn) { cards.forEach(c => fn(c)); }
function render() {
  const pp = p;
  // headline runs right across the page in opposite directions
  const rise = 1 - out(span(pp, 0, .12));
  const run = mix(-50, 76, span(pp, 0, .58));
  $('l1').style.transform = `translate3d(${run}vw,${rise * 34}vh,0)`;
  $('l2').style.transform = `translate3d(${-run}vw,${rise * 34}vh,0)`;
  const capA = 1 - span(pp, .52, .57);
  $('cap').style.opacity = capA; $('cap').style.transform = `translate(-50%,calc(-50% + ${rise * 34}vh))`;
  const intro = 1 - span(pp, 0, .05);
  for (const id of ['hint', 'pager', 'cross', 'glow']) $(id).style.opacity = intro;
  $('rule').style.transform = `scaleX(${ease(span(pp, .72, .86))})`;
  $('rule').style.top = '50%';
  // ribbon, then the grid
  const pr = span(pp, RIB_A, RIB_B), head = mix(0, PATH_L + cards.length * STEP, pr);
  for (const c of cards) {
    const s = head - c.i * STEP, end = PATH_L - CARD_W;
    if (s < end) {
      c.mesh.visible = s > CARD_W; c.rect = null;
      if (c.mesh.visible) poseRibbon(c, head);
    } else if (c.i < cols * rows) {
      // each card flies to its slot the moment it leaves the rail
      const st = mix(RIB_A, RIB_B, (end + c.i * STEP) / (PATH_L + cards.length * STEP)), q = out(span(pp, st, st + .13));
      c.mesh.visible = q > .001;
      if (c.mesh.visible) poseGrid(c, q);
    } else { c.mesh.visible = false; c.rect = null; }
  }
  renderer.render(scene, camera);
}

/* ---------- hover ---------- */
const nameEl = $('name');
$('stage').addEventListener('pointermove', e => {
  let hit = null;
  if (p > .86) {
    const nx = (e.clientX / W - .5), ny = (.5 - e.clientY / H);
    for (const c of cards) { const g = c.rect; if (!g) continue; const x = nx * g.vw, y = ny * g.vh; if (Math.abs(x - g.x) < g.w / 2 && Math.abs(y - g.y) < g.h / 2) hit = c; }
  }
  nameEl.style.opacity = hit ? 1 : 0;
  if (hit) { nameEl.textContent = hit.title; nameEl.style.transform = `translate(${e.clientX + 14}px,${e.clientY + 16}px)`; }
});

/* ---------- loop ---------- */
function loop() {
  if (!frozen) {
    p += (target - p) * .09;
    if (Math.abs(target - p) < .00005) p = target;
    for (const c of cards) {
      if (c.mesh.visible && c.v.paused) c.v.play().catch(() => {});
      else if (!c.mesh.visible && !c.v.paused) c.v.pause();
    }
    render();
  }
  requestAnimationFrame(loop);
}
loop();
~~~

## 12. Feel

Black, quiet and exact. The headline glides like two trains passing. The ribbon arrives small and far away, then swings past you with real weight, wraps around the edge and is gone. Then six live pieces of work settle into a calm grid.
```

```markdown
# Lumen Roof — Morning / Night Fog Hero (exact recreation prompt)

Give me a single-file, full-viewport solar company hero called **Lumen Roof**. A charcoal farmhouse with solar panels fills the screen under a big centred headline. A glass Morning / Night toggle sits at the bottom. Clicking it sinks the whole house about a quarter of the screen into rising fog, swaps the time of day while it is hidden, and floats the house back up in the new light, while the sky, fog colour, nav, headline and button change with it.

Plain HTML, CSS and one vanilla script with raw WebGL2 in one file, with no libraries. The only external resources are the Google Font and the six image URLs below. Reproduce every value, string and timing exactly, and use the complete code at the end as the source of truth.

Six rules define it:
1. **Three layers, one moving.** A blurred sky stays still. The house and its garden sit in one layer that moves on the Y axis only. Fog is a live shader canvas above both, and all text sits above the fog.
2. **Two images make the moving layer.** The full photo is masked so only its lower part shows (the ground and shrubs). The transparent house cutout sits on top of it, so the house's outline stays clean against the blurred sky.
3. **The swap happens at the deepest point.** Fog fully covers the roof at that moment, so the change of house is never seen.
4. **Everything is driven by one clock.** There are no CSS transitions on the scene. One `requestAnimationFrame` function computes sink, fog surge and colours from the time since the click and writes them to CSS variables and shader uniforms.
5. **Colours are mixed, not swapped.** Every text colour is a `color-mix()` on `--k`, where 0 is morning and 1 is night.
6. **No video.** The fog is a generated shader, so it moves forever and never loops.

---

## 1. Page basics

- Title: `Lumen Roof`
- Meta description: `Forget the energy market, weather conditions and seasons. Our Smart Controller guarantees you get no electricity bill for seven years.`
- Font: `https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=Instrument+Sans:wght@400;500;600&display=swap`, with preconnects to fonts.googleapis.com and fonts.gstatic.com (crossorigin). The supplied standalone file embeds the latin woff2 as base64 instead.
- `html`, `body` and `.hero` background `#0b1426`. `.hero` is `100svh` tall with `min-height:520px`, `overflow:hidden` and `isolation:isolate`. Body has `overflow:hidden`.
- The unit for all desktop sizes is `--u:min(calc(100vw/1600),calc(100vh/900))`. It becomes `1px` at 820px wide and below.
- The page starts on **Night**: `--k:1`, the night set visible and the Night button pressed.

## 2. Images (use these exact URLs)

All are served through images.higgs.ai as webp and are `object-fit:cover; object-position:50% 62%`.

1. Morning sky, blurred, no house (w=1600, q=80): `https://images.higgs.ai/?default=1&output=webp&url=https%3A%2F%2Fd8j0ntlcm91z4.cloudfront.net%2Fuser_38xzZboKViGWJOttwIXH07lWA1P%2Fhf_20261102_040343_a73684b4-3f71-4613-a843-c8be80fb1211.png&w=1600&q=80`
2. Night sky, blurred, no house (w=1600, q=80): `https://images.higgs.ai/?default=1&output=webp&url=https%3A%2F%2Fd8j0ntlcm91z4.cloudfront.net%2Fuser_38xzZboKViGWJOttwIXH07lWA1P%2Fhf_20261102_040308_f31964ab-ed8e-4ea4-90eb-3226c0859936.png&w=1600&q=80`
3. Morning full photo, used for ground (w=2560, q=85): `https://images.higgs.ai/?default=1&output=webp&url=https%3A%2F%2Fd8j0ntlcm91z4.cloudfront.net%2Fuser_38xzZboKViGWJOttwIXH07lWA1P%2Fhf_20261102_040259_1be34093-835e-4de4-b3a8-f875e6a74591.png&w=2560&q=85`
4. Morning house cutout, transparent (w=2560, q=85): `https://images.higgs.ai/?default=1&output=webp&url=https%3A%2F%2Fd8j0ntlcm91z4.cloudfront.net%2Fuser_38xzZboKViGWJOttwIXH07lWA1P%2Fhf_20261102_040416_e3b05fa4-cc80-4a43-afde-8a0a053933e9.png&w=2560&q=85`
5. Night full photo, used for ground (w=2560, q=85): `https://images.higgs.ai/?default=1&output=webp&url=https%3A%2F%2Fd8j0ntlcm91z4.cloudfront.net%2Fuser_38xzZboKViGWJOttwIXH07lWA1P%2Fhf_20261102_040211_c8fd4865-285e-4c1f-8a37-4bfe0771357b.png&w=2560&q=85`
6. Night house cutout, transparent (w=2560, q=85): `https://images.higgs.ai/?default=1&output=webp&url=https%3A%2F%2Fd8j0ntlcm91z4.cloudfront.net%2Fuser_38xzZboKViGWJOttwIXH07lWA1P%2Fhf_20261102_040415_2ab95096-8c39-449f-b36c-17c2813815a4.png&w=2560&q=85`

## 3. Layer stack, bottom to top

1. `.sky`: morning image with the night image on top. Both have `filter:blur(calc(7*var(--u)))` and `transform:scale(1.05)`. The night image has `opacity:var(--k)`, so the sky blends in step with the text.
2. `.home`: full-screen layer with `transform:translate3d(0,var(--sink,0px),0)` and `will-change:transform`. It holds `#setM` and `#setN`, of which only `.is-on` is visible (`visibility`). Each set is a `.ground` layer with the full photo under `mask-image:linear-gradient(transparent 54%,#000 64%)`, then the cutout at full size.
3. `.tilt`: `backdrop-filter:blur(calc(9*var(--u)))` masked with `linear-gradient(transparent 70%,#000 92%)`, which softens the foreground like a tilt-shift lens.
4. `#fog`: the WebGL2 canvas, `pointer-events:none`.
5. `.ui`: all text and buttons, `z-index:2`.

## 4. Content

- Logo: 12-ray sun, each ray `M18.3 3.5h3.4l.9 8.4h-5.2Z` rotated in 30° steps about (20,20) in a 40 viewBox, 38u wide, filled with `color-mix(in srgb,#6d8f2a calc((1 - var(--k))*100%),#d8ee8e)`. Wordmark `Lumen Roof`, 25u, weight 500, letter spacing -.025em, gap 9u.
- Nav, centred: `How It Works`, `Our Cases`, `About Us`, `Careers`, `Resources`, 16.5u, weight 500, gap 42u.
- Right side: `Customers`, then the pill button `Get an Instant Quote`, 46u tall, 26u side padding, radius 99px. Black `#0d1117` with white text in the morning, white with `#0d1117` text at night, mixed on `--k`. It lifts 1px on hover.
- Bar padding: 22u top, 38u sides. Logo and right side are `flex:1 1 0` so the links stay truly centred.
- Headline, 58u below the bar, 64u, line height 1.09, weight 500, letter spacing -.022em: `$0 Electricity Bills` / `for the next 7 Years`.
- Headline colour `--ink` mixes `#14202f` to `#fff`. `for the next` uses `--k2` and a muted `#7c8794` tone in the morning, so it is two-tone by day and all white by night, exactly like the reference's split headline.
- Toggle, 524u × 86u, radius 16u, 2u padding, `rgba(120,132,140,.34)` with a `rgba(255,255,255,.2)` border and `backdrop-filter:blur(14u)`. Two equal buttons: `Morning` and `Night`, each 23u weight 500 with `$0 for Electricity` under it at 15u, 72% opacity.
- The active button shows a `:before` with `linear-gradient(160deg,#f7f8dc,#e2ee9f 90%)` and `box-shadow:inset 0 0 18u rgba(255,255,255,.65)`. Its opacity is `--on`, which is `1 - k` on Morning and `k` on Night, so the two buttons crossfade rather than slide. Label colour mixes `#1c2316` and `#fff` on `--on`.
- Caption, 22u below the toggle, 16.4u, line height 1.3, colour `--soft`: `Forget the energy market, weather conditions and seasons. Our Smart` line break `Controller guarantees you get no electricity bill for seven years.` Dock has 40u bottom padding.

## 5. The switch

Constants: `SINK=240`, `RISE=820`, `DEPTH=.27`. With `d` as milliseconds since the click:

- **Sink:** for `d<SINK`, `y = x*x*(3-2*x)*DEPTH` with `x=d/SINK`.
- **Swap:** the first frame with `d>=SINK` swaps the visible house set.
- **Rise:** `y = Math.pow(1-x,3.4)*DEPTH` with `x=(d-SINK)/RISE`.
- `--sink` is `y*innerHeight` in px.
- **Fog surge:** `s = smooth(0,SINK*.92,d) * (1-smooth(SINK+70,SINK+RISE*.92,d))`.
- **UI dip:** `dip = smooth(30,190,d) * (1-smooth(330,720,d))`. Nav links, `Customers` and the headline's first line and `7 Years` fade by 80–82%, and the button by 62%. `for the next` stays solid, as it does in the reference.
- **Colours:** `k` moves from its start to the target on `smooth(120,520,d)`. `k2` does the same on `smooth(340,760,d)`.
- At `d>=SINK+RISE` the animation ends. A click during the animation is queued and runs next, unless it matches the current target.
- With `prefers-reduced-motion` the state changes instantly.
- Buttons are real `<button>` elements with `aria-pressed`, inside `role="group" aria-label="Time of day"`, with a 2px white focus ring.

## 6. Fog shader

A fragment shader on one fullscreen triangle, rendered at no more than 960px wide (upscaled by CSS), with `premultipliedAlpha:true`. Uniforms: `R` size, `T` seconds, `S` surge, `K` night amount.

- Five-octave value-noise `fbm`, rotated first by `mat2(.8,.6,-.6,.8)` and offset by 5.3 so no grid shows, then by `mat2(1.6,1.2,-1.2,1.6)` for each octave.
- Time is `T*.05`. Domain warp `w`, then density `d`, then a slower `e`.
- Resting fog is three parts added together: `low` along the bottom (`smoothstep(.70,1.04,y+(d-.5)*.34)`), `side` on the left and right edges at 20% strength, and `wisps` in mid-air at 18%.
- Surge: fog front at `1.02-S*.68`, with `rise = smoothstep(front-.02,front+.26,y+(d-.5)*.5)`, plus overall `haze = S*(.3+.46*d)`.
- Alpha is the largest of resting fog, `rise*.97` and `haze`.
- Colour is mixed by density: morning `(.79,.78,.71)` to `(.97,.93,.84)`, night `(.15,.19,.29)` to `(.40,.45,.57)`, blended by `K`.
- At night a warm amber `(.86,.55,.27)` glow spot at (.72,.74) tints the fog by the porch, at 42%, and it disappears during a surge.

## 7. Phones (820px and below)

`--u:1px`, nav links and `Customers` hidden, bar padding 16px, logo 21px, button 40px tall. Headline `clamp(34px,10.4vw,56px)`. Images shift to `object-position:72% 62%` so the panels and porch stay in frame. Toggle is full width up to 440px and 74px tall, labels 19px and 13px. Caption is 14px with its line break removed.

<script>
const root=document.documentElement.style,$=id=>document.getElementById(id);
const calm=matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion:reduce)').matches;
const SINK=240,RISE=820,DEPTH=.27;
const clamp=(x,a=0,b=1)=>Math.min(b,Math.max(a,x));
const smooth=(a,b,x)=>{x=clamp((x-a)/(b-a));return x*x*(3-2*x)};
let night=1,target=1,from=1,start=-1e9,queued=null,swapped=true,k=1,surge=0;

const cv=$('fog'),gl=cv.getContext('webgl2',{alpha:true,premultipliedAlpha:true,antialias:false});
let U={};
if(gl){
  const vs=`#version 300 es
  void main(){vec2 p=vec2((gl_VertexID<<1)&2,gl_VertexID&2);gl_Position=vec4(p*2.-1.,0,1);}`;
  const fs=`#version 300 es
  precision highp float;
  uniform vec2 R;uniform float T,S,K;out vec4 O;
  float h(vec2 p){p=fract(p*vec2(123.34,456.21));p+=dot(p,p+45.32);return fract(p.x*p.y);}
  float n(vec2 p){vec2 i=floor(p),f=fract(p);f=f*f*(3.-2.*f);
    return mix(mix(h(i),h(i+vec2(1,0)),f.x),mix(h(i+vec2(0,1)),h(i+vec2(1,1)),f.x),f.y);}
  float fbm(vec2 p){float a=.5,s=0.;mat2 m=mat2(1.6,1.2,-1.2,1.6);p=mat2(.8,.6,-.6,.8)*p+5.3;for(int i=0;i<5;i++){s+=a*n(p);p=m*p;a*=.5;}return s;}
  void main(){
    vec2 uv=gl_FragCoord.xy/R;uv.y=1.-uv.y;
    float asp=R.x/R.y;vec2 p=vec2(uv.x*asp,uv.y);
    float t=T*.05;
    vec2 w=vec2(fbm(p*1.3+vec2(t,-t*.6)),fbm(p*1.3+vec2(-t*.8,t)+7.));
    float d=fbm(p*1.9+w*1.7+vec2(t*1.6,-t*1.1+S*.5));
    float e=fbm(p*.9-w+vec2(-t,t*.5)+3.);
    float low=smooth2(.70,1.04,uv.y+(d-.5)*.34);
    float side=smooth2(.2,.0,uv.x+(e-.5)*.28)+smooth2(.8,1.,uv.x+(e-.5)*.28);
    side*=smooth2(.25,.6,uv.y)*.2;
    float wisps=smooth2(.5,.78,d)*smooth2(.22,.5,uv.y)*smooth2(.86,.6,uv.y)*.18;
    float rest=clamp(low+side+wisps,0.,1.);
    float front=1.02-S*.68;
    float rise=smooth2(front-.02,front+.26,uv.y+(d-.5)*.5);
    float haze=S*(.3+.46*d);
    float a=clamp(max(rest,max(rise*.97,haze)),0.,1.);
    vec3 dayA=vec3(.97,.93,.84),dayB=vec3(.79,.78,.71);
    vec3 nitA=vec3(.40,.45,.57),nitB=vec3(.15,.19,.29);
    vec3 c=mix(mix(dayB,dayA,d*1.15),mix(nitB,nitA,d*1.1),K);
    float porch=exp(-dot((uv-vec2(.72,.74))*vec2(1.7,2.6),(uv-vec2(.72,.74))*vec2(1.7,2.6))*3.2);
    c=mix(c,vec3(.86,.55,.27),K*porch*.42*(1.-S));
    O=vec4(c*a,a);
  }`.replace(/smooth2/g,'smoothstep');
  const sh=(t,s)=>{const o=gl.createShader(t);gl.shaderSource(o,s);gl.compileShader(o);
    if(!gl.getShaderParameter(o,gl.COMPILE_STATUS))console.error(gl.getShaderInfoLog(o));return o};
  const pr=gl.createProgram();gl.attachShader(pr,sh(gl.VERTEX_SHADER,vs));gl.attachShader(pr,sh(gl.FRAGMENT_SHADER,fs));
  gl.linkProgram(pr);gl.useProgram(pr);
  for(const u of['R','T','S','K'])U[u]=gl.getUniformLocation(pr,u);
}
function size(){
  if(!gl)return;
  const w=Math.round(Math.min(innerWidth,960)),h=Math.round(w*innerHeight/innerWidth);
  if(cv.width!==w||cv.height!==h){cv.width=w;cv.height=h;gl.viewport(0,0,w,h)}
}
addEventListener('resize',size);size();

function show(n){
  $('setM').classList.toggle('is-on',!n);$('setN').classList.toggle('is-on',!!n);
}
function pick(n){
  if(n===target&&queued===null)return;
  $('bm').setAttribute('aria-pressed',!n);$('bn').setAttribute('aria-pressed',!!n);
  if(calm){target=night=n;k=n;show(n);return}
  if(animating)queued=n;else begin(n,clock);
}
let animating=false,clock=0;
function begin(n,now){target=n;from=k;start=now;swapped=false;animating=true}
$('bm').onclick=()=>pick(0);$('bn').onclick=()=>pick(1);

function frame(now){
  clock=now;
  const d=now-start;let y=0,s=0,dip=0,k2=k;
  if(animating){
    if(d<SINK){const x=d/SINK;y=x*x*(3-2*x)*DEPTH}
    else{
      if(!swapped){swapped=true;night=target;show(target)}
      const x=clamp((d-SINK)/RISE);y=Math.pow(1-x,3.4)*DEPTH;
    }
    s=smooth(0,SINK*.92,d)*(1-smooth(SINK+70,SINK+RISE*.92,d));
    dip=smooth(30,190,d)*(1-smooth(330,720,d));
    k=from+(target-from)*smooth(120,520,d);
    k2=from+(target-from)*smooth(340,760,d);
    if(d>=SINK+RISE){animating=false;k=k2=target;y=s=dip=0;if(queued!==null&&queued!==target){const q=queued;queued=null;begin(q,now)}else queued=null}
  }
  root.setProperty('--sink',(y*innerHeight).toFixed(1)+'px');
  root.setProperty('--k',k.toFixed(3));root.setProperty('--k2',k2.toFixed(3));root.setProperty('--dip',dip.toFixed(3));
  if(gl){gl.uniform2f(U.R,cv.width,cv.height);gl.uniform1f(U.T,now/1000);gl.uniform1f(U.S,s);gl.uniform1f(U.K,k);gl.drawArrays(gl.TRIANGLES,0,3)}
}
function loop(t){frame(t);requestAnimationFrame(loop)}
requestAnimationFrame(loop);
</script>
</body>
</html>
~~~
```

```markdown
==================================================
5. PRISM + LIGHT ENGINE (<script type="module">)
==================================================
Import map: "three": "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.160.0/build/three.module.js", "three/addons/": "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.160.0/examples/jsm/". Add a header comment crediting the glass as ported from vercel-labs/vgpu (MIT License, Copyright (c) Vercel, Inc.), apps/docs/app/[lang]/(home)/components/prism-background.

5a. Layout (in CSS px, recomputed on resize, debounced 60ms, and after document.fonts.ready)
- W,H = stage size. dpr = min(devicePixelRatio,2). mobile = W < 820. Light canvases use dpr (mobile: min(dpr,1.5)).
- Desktop: side S = min(W*0.36, H*0.62), centroid at (0.66W, 0.53H).
- Mobile: S = min(W*0.72, H*0.40, 400); centroid x = W/2, y = max(copyBottom+30 + S*0.62, (copyBottom+30+H)/2).
- 2D "light plane" triangle (y down): top (cx, cy−R), right (cx+S/2, cy+R/2), left (cx−S/2, cy+R/2), R = S/√3. Edges: 0 = right face (top→right), 1 = base, 2 = left face. Outward edge normals.

5b. Optics (2D ray tracing on the plane through the middle of the glass)
- Dispersion (Cauchy): n(λ) = 1.2 + 0.1/λ² (λ in µm). 72 wavelengths from 410 to 695 nm.
- Colour per λ via a piecewise visible-spectrum approximation (violet/blue <440, blue→cyan to 490, cyan→green to 510, green→yellow to 580, yellow→red to 645, red after). Store a "vivid" RGB for fills, and a white-balanced RGB+weight (sum of all wavelengths = white) for core lines.
- Per wavelength: trace from the lamp; at every face apply vector Snell refraction; unpolarised Fresnel split (rs,rp averaged); total internal reflection when Snell has no solution. Recurse up to depth 7; continue transmitted rays if energy > 0.08, reflected if > 0.12. Rays leaving the prism go 1.5×diagonal far. Group segments of all wavelengths by their path key (sequence of T/R + face) so neighbouring wavelengths can be filled into a continuous band.
- Lamp (vgpu lampForIncidence): always from the RIGHT, aimed at a point on the right face. Incidence angle from pointer height y∈[0,1]: piecewise −35° (top) → 60° (middle) → 75° (bottom). Direction = inward normal of the right face rotated by +incidence (y-down space). Entry point = lerp along right face from 0.08 to 0.92 by pointer x. Source = entry − dir × far.

5c. Drawing the light (offscreen 2D canvas, additive 'lighter')
- Incoming beam: white stroke 12px @ .3 alpha + 4.5px @ 1 (×0.8 on mobile), round caps.
- 70 dust motes drifting along the incoming beam (spread wider away from the prism), radius .5–1.6, twinkling alpha .3–1 × .75.
- For each path group: per wavelength a white-balanced core line (alpha = weight × energy × 2.2, width 4 inside / 3.4 outside); between neighbouring wavelengths fill a quad with the vivid colour (alpha energy × .5 inside, × .78 outside). Outgoing quads use a linear gradient alpha 1 → .75 (30%) → .25 (70%) → 0.
- Edge glints: where the beam crosses a face, stroke that whole face with a radial white gradient (radius 0.2·S) 2px wide, plus a 2.6px white dot.
- Soft bloom composite into #fx: drawImage the offscreen canvas three times with ctx.filter blur(34px)@.6, blur(12px)@.9, blur(3.2px)@1 — no unblurred pass (everything soft). If canvas filters are unsupported, fake the blur by drawing through 1/16, 1/6 and 1/2 size buffers and scaling up.
- All plane points are mapped to the screen through the 3D camera each frame (so the light gets the same subtle parallax as the glass).

5d. The 3D glass (three.js 0.160, WebGL2 required; otherwise hide nothing and fall back to the 2D #fx canvas with a thin triangle outline)
- Renderer: antialias, autoClear false, outputColorSpace Linear, NoToneMapping (shaders encode sRGB themselves). Hide #fx; use it as a CanvasTexture (needsUpdate every frame).
- Constants (vgpu, side 0.57 units): depth = S × 0.3/0.57, fillet radius = S × 0.008/0.57 on ALL nine edges, 4 corner segments, 4 bevel segments, 16 edge segments. Port vgpu's prismMeshData: rounded-triangle contour (tangent arcs at corners), quarter-round rings (theta stops at π/2−0.06) from back cap to front cap, then front/back cap fans. Interleaved position+normal, Uint16 indices, apex up, centred at origin, z ∈ [−depth/2, +depth/2].
- Five ideal planes (3 side faces + front + back) as (outward normal, offset) uniforms.
- Camera: PerspectiveCamera fov 48°, distance D = (H/2)/tan(24°) so z=0 maps 1:1 to CSS px; it orbits on a sphere around the prism by up to ±3.5° yaw/pitch from the pointer and always looks at the prism; camera.setViewOffset(W,H, W/2−cx, H/2−cy, W,H) keeps the prism at its layout position.
- Studio environment (analytic, in the shader — vgpu environment.wgsl): near-black room with darker back wall (−z) and slightly lighter floor; + back-left wall panel dir(−0.82,0.08,0.57) size(1.35,1.1) feather .22 colour(.82,.84,.88) ×0.011; + soft fill dir(0,−0.707,0.707) size(.38,.62) feather .18 colour(1,.97,.91) ×0.22; + cool right key dir(0.612,0.354,0.707) size(.5,.16) feather .035 colour(.76,.88,1) ×20. Then c/(1+c), pow 1/2.2, sRGB→linear, × exposure 2.3.
- Glass params (dark theme): IOR 1.645, F0 = ((ior−1)/(ior+1))², reflectionStrength 2.14, Beer–Lambert absorption (1,1,0.54) per 0.57-unit side (scale by 0.57/S per px), Schlick Fresnel.
- Render order each frame:
  1. Into a HalfFloat render target: full-screen quad = page bg #151517 screen-blended with the light canvas (1−(1−bg)(1−rgb·a)), stored linear.
  2. Back faces (BackSide, premultiplied blend ONE / ONE_MINUS_SRC_ALPHA) — vgpu glass-back.wgsl: refract camera ray glass→air at the inward normal; on TIR reflect and continue to the next ideal plane (exclude the plane just left), up to 3 bounces. Also follow the inner-face reflection out of the glass, sample the studio, × (1−Fresnel) at its exit. Output (env × reflection × weight, weight), weight = Fresnel if escaped else 1.
  3. To screen: copy the render target (linear→sRGB).
  4. Front faces — vgpu glass.wgsl: reflect view ray → studio; refract into glass (1/ior), march to the nearest ideal plane, project that exit point with a uViewProj uniform to UV, sample the render target, × exp(−absorption·distance). colour = transmitted·(1−F) + reflected·F + panel highlight (smoothstep(.5,.82, luminance(env)) × clamp(reflection·.4,0,.7) × (.65+.35·(1−facing)^1.5)). Soft shoulder above 0.8 instead of ACES, then linear→sRGB.
  (GLSL: no ternary on structs; projectionMatrix isn't available in fragment shaders — pass a uViewProj uniform.)

5e. Interaction (vgpu interaction.ts)
- Normalised pointer over the stage: height → incidence (aim[0]), width → entry point (aim[1]); camera orbit target = (x·2−1, y·2−1). Ease per 60Hz frame: lamp 0.12, camera 0.08 (frame-rate independent). Pointer leaving the window → orbit back to 0.
- Mobile (and an idle desktop after 6s without movement): a virtual pointer circles the centre, radius 0.34, period 18s (no camera orbit on mobile). Respect prefers-reduced-motion (no automatic motion).
- Listen to pointermove (primary only), pointerdown and touchmove (passive).

Result: a dark-gray page, the serif "halo" wordmark and Geist headline on the left, and on the right a smoky, slightly rounded 3D glass prism. A soft white beam with dust comes in from the right, refracts through the glass and fans out to the left as a wide, smooth, glowing rainbow. Moving the mouse swings the light and tilts the view.
```

### [FREE-156] Jellyfish Scroll (`driftlab-hero`)
- **Danh mục:** Interactive | **Loại:** hero | **Độ dài:** 25,106 ký tự
- **Video Preview:** https://pub-86dc5b5484314368ac5436a674b0d919.r2.dev/aaaf/driftlab-hero.mp4
- **Poster 1280px:** https://images.higgs.ai/?default=1&output=webp&url=https%3A%2F%2Fd8j0ntlcm91z4.cloudfront.net%2Fuser_38xzZboKViGWJOttwIXH07lWA1P%2Fhf_20261102_053925_7184163c-7d4f-4bc9-94ef-a11bfadb6a35.png&w=1280&q=85

```markdown
# Driftlab — Jellyfish Scroll Hero (exact recreation prompt)

Give me a single-file, scroll-driven hero called **Driftlab**. A pink jellyfish floats in the middle of a lilac sky. Huge condensed black words arrive big from the lower right on a curve, pass behind the jellyfish, pause in the centre and leave to the left. After the last word falls away, the jellyfish grows and two text panels appear in turn while it moves to the other side.

Plain HTML, CSS and one vanilla script with raw WebGL2 in one file, with no libraries. The only external resources are the Google Fonts and the three media URLs below. Reproduce every value, string and timing exactly, and use the complete code at the end as the source of truth.

Six rules define it:
1. **One canvas, drawn in this order:** sky, points, words, jellyfish. Depth is simply draw order, which is why the jellyfish is always in front of the letters.
2. **The jellyfish is a green-screen video keyed in a shader.** `d = g - max(r,b)` and `alpha = 1 - smoothstep(.10,.38,d)`. Green spill is clamped with `g = min(g, max(r,b)*.96)`. Translucent tentacles keep the letters visible through them.
3. **Words are bent ribbons.** Each word is a 56-column triangle strip on a ring of radius 9. Its ends come towards the camera and its right side drops, which gives the big entrance from the lower right.
4. **The words share one atlas.** Each word is drawn once with Canvas 2D into its own 512px row of a 4096px texture, with mipmaps and anisotropic filtering.
5. **Words dwell.** Position between words uses `ease = x*x*x*(x*(6*x-15)+10)`, so each one rests in the centre.
6. **A sticky stage on a long page.** `.track` is 800vh and `.view` is sticky. The script reads scroll progress and eases towards it at 10% per frame.

---

## 1. Page basics

- Title: `Driftlab`
- Meta description: `A jellyfish drifts through a lilac sky while huge words wrap around it as you scroll.`
- Fonts: `https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=Anton&family=Outfit:wght@600&family=Space+Mono&display=swap`, with preconnects to fonts.googleapis.com and fonts.gstatic.com (crossorigin). The supplied standalone file embeds the latin woff2 files as base64 instead.
- Anton for the giant words, caption and panels. Outfit 600 for the logo. Space Mono for links, index and the sound label.
- Ink `#0b0b10`, page fallback `#dcd8f4`.
- Unit: `--u:min(calc(100vw/1600),calc(100vh/900))`, which becomes `1px` at 820px wide and below.

## 2. Media (use these exact URLs)

All three are served with `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *`. Load them with `crossOrigin='anonymous'`.

1. Sky (w=1920, q=80): `https://images.higgs.ai/?default=1&output=webp&url=https%3A%2F%2Fd8j0ntlcm91z4.cloudfront.net%2Fuser_38xzZboKViGWJOttwIXH07lWA1P%2Fhf_20261102_045255_3cb4b3c2-3cb5-4af9-93b4-bd88f2f883c3.png&w=1920&q=80`
2. Jellyfish still on green, shown until the video has a frame and used alone for reduced motion (w=1080, q=85): `https://images.higgs.ai/?default=1&output=webp&url=https%3A%2F%2Fd8j0ntlcm91z4.cloudfront.net%2Fuser_38xzZboKViGWJOttwIXH07lWA1P%2Fhf_20261102_045249_4f7fe287-c84b-479f-a953-04990fe1a3ac.png&w=1080&q=85`
3. Jellyfish video on green, 1080 × 1920, 5 s seamless loop, muted, looping, inline, `preload="auto"`, not added to the page: `https://d8j0ntlcm91z4.cloudfront.net/user_38xzZboKViGWJOttwIXH07lWA1P/hf_20261102_045327_a6584765-3154-43e6-b1c9-4e574f83a811.mp4`

## 3. Overlay content

- Logo top left at 30u, 20u: `Driftlab`, Outfit 600, 25u, followed by a 50u wide hand-drawn squiggle SVG.
- Top right at 38u, 24u: `[Works]` and `[Agency]`, 13u, gap 18u.
- Left index, centred at 19u from the left: rows of 3u dots with `01`, `02`, `03`, `04`, `05` between them, 11u. The current word's number is at full opacity, the others at 45%.
- Right edge at 10u: a 1px scroll rail from 22% to 78% of the height, with a 3px thumb 9% tall.
- Bottom centre, 680u wide, 30u from the bottom: a goggles icon, 30u × 20u, above Anton 23u uppercase captions at line height 1.18.
- First caption: `Welcome to a creative space showcasing groundbreaking` / `projects that blend creativity and technology`
- Second caption: `Follow us into the future of interactive` / `and immersive digital experiences`
- Left panel at 84u: `Each project at Driftlab serves as a testament to our commitment to innovation and excellence`
- Right panel at 84u, right aligned: `Browse our portfolio to see the magic we create with cutting-edge technologies including XR, AR, AI and 3D.`
- Panels are 330u wide, Anton 25u, line height 1.14, vertically centred, rising 18px as they fade in.
- Bottom left: black 30u sound pill with seven small bars and `OFF` or `ON`. It plays looping brown noise through a 520 Hz lowpass with a .09 Hz wobble of ±240 Hz, fading to .34 gain.
- Bottom right: 34u black circle with an up arrow that scrolls back to the top.

## 4. Scroll timeline

With `s` from 0 to 1, and `span = .14 * 4 = .56`:

- **Words:** `k = clamp(s/span)*4`. The head position moves between word centres with the ease above.
- **Sink:** from `span+.015` to `span+.105`, the words drop by 6 units.
- **Grow:** from `span+.08` to `span+.22`, the jellyfish grows from .98 to 1.40 of its base height and moves down .1.
- **Side:** `smooth(.76,.82,s) - 2*smooth(.88,.94,s)`, moving the jellyfish by `.34` clip units, right for the left panel and left for the right panel.
- **First caption:** fades out from .04 to .08. **Second caption:** in from .08 to .12, out from .56 to .62. The goggles follow whichever is showing.
- **Left panel:** in .72–.77, out .84–.88. **Right panel:** in .90–.95, then stays.

## 5. Word ribbons

Constants: `GAP=3.4`, `RADIUS=9`, `CAM=11`, `FOCAL=8.14`. Words in order: `DRIFTLAB`, `DESIGN TO`, `DELIGHT`, `INSPIRE`, `AND ENGAGE`. Anton 440px with 8px letter spacing, each word's world length being its measured width / 440 × .86.

For a vertex at track position `t` from the centre:

~~~
th = clamp(t/9, -1.45, 1.45)
x  = 9*sin(th)
z  = 9*(1-cos(th))*.82
y  = (v-.5)*height + .19 - sink - 3.6*pow(smoothstep(.8,8.,t),1.25) - .012*t*t
gl_Position = vec4(x*8.14/aspect, y*8.14, 0, 11-z)
~~~

Using `w = 11-z` makes the perspective correct on the texture. The colour is `(.043,.043,.063)`, premultiplied. On narrow screens everything is scaled by `clamp(aspect*.58,.26,1)`.

## 6. Jellyfish

A quad of base height .98 × 2 clip units at 1080:1920, scaled by `clamp(.62+aspect*.4,.6,1)` on narrow screens. It bobs `.018*sin(t*.8)`, follows the mouse by .018, rolls by `.1*sin(s*13+.4) + .03*sin(t*.5)`, and squashes its width by `.93+.07*cos(s*14)` to suggest turning. The matrix corrects for aspect so rotation never skews it.

## 7. Sky and points

- The sky is drawn at mip level 1.6 for softness, cover-fitted at 92% zoom, and drifts sideways by `s*.05 + t*.0022`.
- 40 points: three quarters are soft white specks, a quarter are black rotating squares that slide with the scroll.

## 8. Phones (820px and below)

`--u:1px`, index hidden, logo 21px, links 12px, caption 17px with its line break removed and 72px from the bottom, panels pinned 72px from the bottom at 21px.

<script>
const SKY='https://images.higgs.ai/?default=1&output=webp&url=https%3A%2F%2Fd8j0ntlcm91z4.cloudfront.net%2Fuser_38xzZboKViGWJOttwIXH07lWA1P%2Fhf_20261102_045255_3cb4b3c2-3cb5-4af9-93b4-bd88f2f883c3.png&w=1920&q=80';
const STILL='https://images.higgs.ai/?default=1&output=webp&url=https%3A%2F%2Fd8j0ntlcm91z4.cloudfront.net%2Fuser_38xzZboKViGWJOttwIXH07lWA1P%2Fhf_20261102_045249_4f7fe287-c84b-479f-a953-04990fe1a3ac.png&w=1080&q=85';

const WORDS=['DRIFTLAB','DESIGN TO','DELIGHT','INSPIRE','AND ENGAGE'];
const STEP=.14,GAP=3.4,RADIUS=9,CAM=11,FOCAL=8.14;
const $=id=>document.getElementById(id),clamp=(x,a=0,b=1)=>Math.min(b,Math.max(a,x));
const smooth=(a,b,x)=>{x=clamp((x-a)/(b-a));return x*x*(3-2*x)},ease=x=>x*x*x*(x*(6*x-15)+10);
const cv=$('gl'),gl=cv.getContext('webgl2',{alpha:false,antialias:true,premultipliedAlpha:true});
const calm=matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion:reduce)').matches;
function program(vs,fs,names){
  const sh=(t,s)=>{const o=gl.createShader(t);gl.shaderSource(o,'#version 300 es\nprecision highp float;\n'+s);gl.compileShader(o);
    if(!gl.getShaderParameter(o,gl.COMPILE_STATUS))console.error(gl.getShaderInfoLog(o));return o};
  const p=gl.createProgram();gl.attachShader(p,sh(gl.VERTEX_SHADER,vs));gl.attachShader(p,sh(gl.FRAGMENT_SHADER,fs));gl.linkProgram(p);
  const u={};names.forEach(n=>u[n]=gl.getUniformLocation(p,n));return{p,u};
}
const QUAD=`out vec2 v;void main(){vec2 c=vec2((gl_VertexID<<1)&2,gl_VertexID&2);v=c;gl_Position=vec4(c*2.-1.,0,1);}`;
const skyP=program(QUAD,`in vec2 v;uniform sampler2D T;uniform vec3 C;out vec4 O;
  void main(){vec2 uv=vec2(.5)+(v-.5)*C.xy;uv.y=1.-uv.y;uv.x+=C.z;O=textureLod(T,uv,1.6);}`,['T','C']);
const wordP=program(`layout(location=0) in vec2 a;uniform vec4 W;uniform vec4 B;uniform float A;uniform vec3 L;out vec2 v;
  void main(){
    float t=(a.x-.5)*W.x+W.y;
    float th=clamp(t/${RADIUS.toFixed(1)},-1.45,1.45);
    float x=${RADIUS.toFixed(1)}*sin(th),z=${RADIUS.toFixed(1)}*(1.-cos(th))*.82;
    float y=(a.y-.5)*L.x+L.y-L.z-3.6*pow(smoothstep(.8,8.,t),1.25)-.012*t*t;
    v=vec2(mix(B.x,B.z,a.x),mix(B.w,B.y,a.y));
    gl_Position=vec4(x*${FOCAL.toFixed(2)}/A,y*${FOCAL.toFixed(2)},0.,${CAM.toFixed(1)}-z);
  }`,`in vec2 v;uniform sampler2D T;out vec4 O;void main(){float a=texture(T,v).a;O=vec4(vec3(.043,.043,.063)*a,a);}`,['W','B','A','L','T']);
const dotP=program(`layout(location=0) in vec4 a;uniform float S,H,P;out float k;out float r;
  void main(){k=a.w;float y=fract(a.y+S*.012*(.4+a.z))*2.3-1.15;float x=fract(a.x+H*(a.w>.5?.035:.004))*2.4-1.2+.03*sin(S*.2+a.z*9.);
    gl_Position=vec4(x,y,0,1);gl_PointSize=(a.w>.5?5.+a.z*15.:5.+a.z*24.)*P;r=S*.6+a.z*7.+H;}`,
  `in float k;in float r;out vec4 O;void main(){vec2 p=gl_PointCoord-.5;
    if(k>.5){float c=cos(r),s=sin(r);p=mat2(c,-s,s,c)*p;float a=step(max(abs(p.x),abs(p.y)),.3);O=vec4(vec3(.04)*a,a);}
    else{float a=smoothstep(.5,.1,length(p))*.62;O=vec4(vec3(1.)*a,a);}}`,['S','H','P']);
const jellyP=program(`uniform mat3 M;out vec2 v;void main(){vec2 c=vec2((gl_VertexID<<1)&2,gl_VertexID&2);if(gl_VertexID==3)c=vec2(2,2);c*=.5;v=vec2(c.x,1.-c.y);gl_Position=vec4((M*vec3(c-.5,1.)).xy,0,1);}`,
  `in vec2 v;uniform sampler2D T;out vec4 O;void main(){
    vec3 c=texture(T,v).rgb;
    float d=c.g-max(c.r,c.b);
    float a=1.-smoothstep(.10,.38,d);
    c.g=min(c.g,max(c.r,c.b)*.96);
    O=vec4(c*a,a);}`,['M','T']);

// word atlas: one row per word, cut to its measured width
const ROW=512,EM=440,atlas=document.createElement('canvas');atlas.width=4096;atlas.height=ROW*WORDS.length;
let layout=[];
function drawAtlas(){
  const x=atlas.getContext('2d');x.clearRect(0,0,atlas.width,atlas.height);x.font=`${EM}px Anton`;x.textBaseline='alphabetic';x.fillStyle='#000';x.textAlign='left';
  x.letterSpacing='8px';let c=0;layout=[];
  WORDS.forEach((w,i)=>{
    const m=x.measureText(w).width+16;x.fillText(w,8,i*ROW+EM*.92+6);
    const uW=m/EM*.86;layout.push({len:uW,c:c+uW/2,u:m/atlas.width,top:i/WORDS.length,bot:(i+1)/WORDS.length});c+=uW+GAP;
  });
}
const tex=(unit,filter)=>{const t=gl.createTexture();gl.activeTexture(gl.TEXTURE0+unit);gl.bindTexture(gl.TEXTURE_2D,t);
  gl.texParameteri(gl.TEXTURE_2D,gl.TEXTURE_WRAP_S,gl.CLAMP_TO_EDGE);gl.texParameteri(gl.TEXTURE_2D,gl.TEXTURE_WRAP_T,gl.CLAMP_TO_EDGE);
  gl.texParameteri(gl.TEXTURE_2D,gl.TEXTURE_MIN_FILTER,filter);gl.texParameteri(gl.TEXTURE_2D,gl.TEXTURE_MAG_FILTER,gl.LINEAR);return t};
const tSky=tex(0,gl.LINEAR_MIPMAP_LINEAR),tWords=tex(1,gl.LINEAR_MIPMAP_LINEAR),tJelly=tex(2,gl.LINEAR);
gl.texImage2D(gl.TEXTURE_2D,0,gl.RGBA,1,1,0,gl.RGBA,gl.UNSIGNED_BYTE,new Uint8Array([0,255,0,255]));
const aniso=gl.getExtension('EXT_texture_filter_anisotropic');
function load(url){return new Promise(r=>{const i=new Image;i.crossOrigin='anonymous';i.onload=()=>r(i);i.onerror=()=>r(null);i.src=url})}

const cols=56,ribbon=new Float32Array((cols+1)*4);
for(let i=0;i<=cols;i++){ribbon.set([i/cols,0,i/cols,1],i*4)}
const vaoW=gl.createVertexArray();gl.bindVertexArray(vaoW);gl.bindBuffer(gl.ARRAY_BUFFER,gl.createBuffer());gl.bufferData(gl.ARRAY_BUFFER,ribbon,gl.STATIC_DRAW);gl.enableVertexAttribArray(0);gl.vertexAttribPointer(0,2,gl.FLOAT,false,0,0);
const dots=[];let sd=7;const rnd=()=>(sd=(sd*16807)%2147483647)/2147483647;
for(let i=0;i<40;i++)dots.push(rnd(),rnd(),rnd(),i%4?0:1);
const vaoD=gl.createVertexArray();gl.bindVertexArray(vaoD);gl.bindBuffer(gl.ARRAY_BUFFER,gl.createBuffer());gl.bufferData(gl.ARRAY_BUFFER,new Float32Array(dots),gl.STATIC_DRAW);gl.enableVertexAttribArray(0);gl.vertexAttribPointer(0,4,gl.FLOAT,false,0,0);
const vaoE=gl.createVertexArray();

const video=document.createElement('video');video.crossOrigin='anonymous';video.muted=true;video.loop=true;video.playsInline=true;video.preload='auto';video.src=VIDEO;
let W=1,H=1,dpr=1,asp=1,haveVid=false,lastT=-1;
function size(){dpr=Math.min(devicePixelRatio||1,2);W=Math.round(cv.clientWidth*dpr);H=Math.round(cv.clientHeight*dpr);cv.width=W;cv.height=H;asp=W/H;gl.viewport(0,0,W,H)}
addEventListener('resize',size);

function pushVideo(){
  if(video.readyState<2||video.currentTime===lastT)return;
  lastT=video.currentTime;haveVid=true;gl.activeTexture(gl.TEXTURE2);gl.bindTexture(gl.TEXTURE_2D,tJelly);gl.pixelStorei(gl.UNPACK_FLIP_Y_WEBGL,false);
  gl.texImage2D(gl.TEXTURE_2D,0,gl.RGBA,gl.RGBA,gl.UNSIGNED_BYTE,video);
}
function draw(s,sec){
  pushVideo();
  const n=WORDS.length,span=STEP*(n-1),k=clamp(s/span)*(n-1),i=Math.min(n-2,Math.floor(k)),f=k-i;
  const c0=layout[i].c,c1=layout[i+1].c,head=c0+(c1-c0)*ease(f);
  const sink=ease(smooth(span+.015,span+.105,s))*6;
  const grow=ease(smooth(span+.08,span+.22,s)),side=smooth(.76,.82,s)-2*smooth(.88,.94,s);
  // sky
  gl.disable(gl.BLEND);gl.useProgram(skyP.p);gl.bindVertexArray(vaoE);
  gl.uniform1i(skyP.u.T,0);const ca=asp/(16/9),fx=ca>1?1:ca,fy=ca>1?1/ca:1;gl.uniform3f(skyP.u.C,fx*.92,fy*.92,s*.05+sec*.0022);gl.drawArrays(gl.TRIANGLES,0,3);
  gl.enable(gl.BLEND);gl.blendFunc(gl.ONE,gl.ONE_MINUS_SRC_ALPHA);
  // points
  gl.useProgram(dotP.p);gl.bindVertexArray(vaoD);gl.uniform1f(dotP.u.S,sec);gl.uniform1f(dotP.u.H,head*.1+s*4);gl.uniform1f(dotP.u.P,dpr*H/dpr/900);gl.drawArrays(gl.POINTS,0,40);
  // words
  gl.useProgram(wordP.p);gl.bindVertexArray(vaoW);gl.uniform1i(wordP.u.T,1);gl.uniform1f(wordP.u.A,asp);
  const hs=clamp(asp*.58,.26,1);gl.uniform3f(wordP.u.L,hs,.19+.1*(1-hs),sink);
  layout.forEach(w=>{const t=w.c-head;if(Math.abs(t)>24)return;
    gl.uniform4f(wordP.u.W,w.len*hs,t*hs,0,0);gl.uniform4f(wordP.u.B,0,w.top,w.u,w.bot);gl.drawArrays(gl.TRIANGLE_STRIP,0,(cols+1)*2)});
  // jellyfish
  gl.useProgram(jellyP.p);gl.bindVertexArray(vaoE);gl.uniform1i(jellyP.u.T,2);
  const h=(.98+grow*.42)*clamp(.62+asp*.4,.6,1),w=h*(1080/1920)/asp*(.93+.07*Math.cos(s*14));
  const roll=(.1*Math.sin(s*13+.4)+.03*Math.sin(sec*.5))*(1+grow*.5),co=Math.cos(roll),si=Math.sin(roll);
  const ox=(mx*.018+side*.34*Math.min(1,asp)),oy=.03+.018*Math.sin(sec*.8)+my*.018-grow*.1;
  gl.uniformMatrix3fv(jellyP.u.M,false,[w*2*co,w*2*si*asp,0,-h*2*si/asp,h*2*co,0,ox,oy,1]);
  gl.drawArrays(gl.TRIANGLE_STRIP,0,4);
  ui(s,k);
}
let lastIdx=0;const marks=[...$('index').querySelectorAll('b')];
function ui(s,k){
  const op=(a,b,c,d)=>smooth(a,b,s)*(1-smooth(c,d,s));
  const c1=1-smooth(.04,.08,s),c2=op(.08,.12,.56,.62);$('c1').style.opacity=c1;$('c2').style.opacity=c2;$('goggle').style.opacity=Math.max(c1,c2);
  const a=op(.72,.77,.84,.88),b=op(.9,.95,1.1,1.2);
  $('p1').style.opacity=a;$('p1').style.transform=`translateY(calc(-50% + ${(1-a)*18}px))`;
  $('p2').style.opacity=b;$('p2').style.transform=`translateY(calc(-50% + ${(1-b)*18}px))`;
  const idx=Math.round(k);if(idx!==lastIdx){marks[lastIdx].classList.remove('on');marks[idx].classList.add('on');lastIdx=idx}
  $('thumb').style.transform=`translateY(${(s*1011).toFixed(1)}%)`;
}

let target=0,now=0,mx=0,my=0,tmx=0,tmy=0;
const read=()=>{const r=$('track').getBoundingClientRect(),m=r.height-innerHeight;target=clamp(-r.top/m)};
addEventListener('scroll',read,{passive:true});
addEventListener('pointermove',e=>{tmx=e.clientX/innerWidth*2-1;tmy=1-e.clientY/innerHeight*2});
function loop(t){
  now+=(target-now)*(calm?1:.1);mx+=(tmx-mx)*.05;my+=(tmy-my)*.05;draw(now,t/1000);
  requestAnimationFrame(loop);
}
$('up').onclick=()=>scrollTo({top:0,behavior:calm?'auto':'smooth'});

let ctx,gain;
$('sound').onclick=()=>{
  const b=$('sound'),on=b.getAttribute('aria-pressed')!=='true';b.setAttribute('aria-pressed',on);$('st').textContent=on?'ON':'OFF';
  if(!ctx){
    ctx=new AudioContext;gain=ctx.createGain();gain.gain.value=0;
    const n=ctx.createBuffer(2,ctx.sampleRate*4,ctx.sampleRate);
    for(let c=0;c<2;c++){const d=n.getChannelData(c);let l=0;for(let i=0;i<d.length;i++){l=(l+.02*(Math.random()*2-1))/1.02;d[i]=l*3.5}}
    const src=ctx.createBufferSource();src.buffer=n;src.loop=true;
    const lp=ctx.createBiquadFilter();lp.type='lowpass';lp.frequency.value=520;
    const lfo=ctx.createOscillator(),lg=ctx.createGain();lfo.frequency.value=.09;lg.gain.value=240;lfo.connect(lg).connect(lp.frequency);
    src.connect(lp).connect(gain).connect(ctx.destination);src.start();lfo.start();
  }
  ctx.resume();gain.gain.setTargetAtTime(on?.34:0,ctx.currentTime,.4);
};

Promise.all([load(SKY),load(STILL),document.fonts.load(`${EM}px Anton`,'DRIFTLAB')]).then(([sky,still])=>{
  drawAtlas();
  gl.activeTexture(gl.TEXTURE0);gl.bindTexture(gl.TEXTURE_2D,tSky);if(sky){gl.pixelStorei(gl.UNPACK_FLIP_Y_WEBGL,false);gl.texImage2D(gl.TEXTURE_2D,0,gl.RGBA,gl.RGBA,gl.UNSIGNED_BYTE,sky);gl.generateMipmap(gl.TEXTURE_2D)}
  gl.activeTexture(gl.TEXTURE1);gl.bindTexture(gl.TEXTURE_2D,tWords);gl.texImage2D(gl.TEXTURE_2D,0,gl.RGBA,gl.RGBA,gl.UNSIGNED_BYTE,atlas);gl.generateMipmap(gl.TEXTURE_2D);
  if(aniso)gl.texParameterf(gl.TEXTURE_2D,aniso.TEXTURE_MAX_ANISOTROPY_EXT,8);
  if(still){gl.activeTexture(gl.TEXTURE2);gl.bindTexture(gl.TEXTURE_2D,tJelly);gl.texImage2D(gl.TEXTURE_2D,0,gl.RGBA,gl.RGBA,gl.UNSIGNED_BYTE,still)}
  if(!calm)video.play().catch(()=>{});
  size();read();now=target;requestAnimationFrame(loop);
});
</script>
</body>
</html>
```

- **Video Preview:** https://pub-86dc5b5484314368ac5436a674b0d919.r2.dev/aaaf/solace-faq.mp4
- **Poster 1280px:** https://images.higgs.ai/?default=1&output=webp&url=https%3A%2F%2Fd8j0ntlcm91z4.cloudfront.net%2Fuser_38xzZboKViGWJOttwIXH07lWA1P%2Fhf_20261103_075712_12a2721b-8989-4660-9a34-bf0707db7779.png&w=1280&q=85

```markdown
# Solace — Halftone Dot FAQ and Footer (exact recreation prompt)

Give me a single-file closing section for an AI co-pilot product called **Solace**. The section runs a FAQ into the footer. Behind both sits a full-width live grid of round amber dots, sparse and ragged at the top and dense and pale lower down. Every dot swells and shrinks at its own pace, so the field ripples like an audio meter, and dots near the cursor swell. A centred heading and a dark amber glass FAQ accordion sit on top, with a full-width brown glass footer panel at the bottom.

Plain HTML, CSS and one vanilla script with a 2D canvas, in one file, with no libraries and no images. The only external resource is the Google Font. Reproduce every value, string and timing exactly, and use the complete code at the end as the source of truth.

---

## 1. Page basics

- Title: `Solace`
- Meta description: `Questions, answered. Solace is your AI co-pilot for the work that matters: priorities, follow-ups and answers across every tool your team already uses.`
- Font: `https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=Geist:wght@400;500;600&display=swap`, with preconnects. The supplied standalone file embeds it.
- Colours: page `#050302`, cream text `#fbefe2`, muted `#d9c3ad`, divider lines `rgba(255,214,170,.14)`, FAQ glass `rgba(34,18,8,.78)`.
- Unit: `--u:min(calc(100vw/1600),calc(100vh/940))`, which becomes `1px` at 820px and below.
- `.wrap` is at least `100svh` with the canvas absolutely filling it. `.content` is a centred flex column with 64u top padding and 28u side and bottom padding.

## 2. Dot field

- Grid step: `max(14, min(W/1600, H/940)*20.5)` px. Each cell gets three stable hash values `a`, `b` and `c` from `fract(sin(i*127.1+j*311.7)*43758.5453)` with offsets.
- Field band: it starts at `H*.1` and is fully dense by `H*.36`. Above `top - 2 steps`, nothing is drawn. Within the band, `v` runs 0 → 1.
- Colour per row: `rgb(226,106,24)` blends to `rgb(248,150,64)` by `v=.55`, then towards `rgb(255,214,170)`, with the last 10% of the height pushing fully to pale peach.
- Survival: `keep = min(1, v*1.6+.12) - a*.6`. A dot with `keep≤0` is skipped unless `c≤.08`, which leaves a few stragglers in the ragged top edge.
- Breathing: `wave = .5+.5*sin(t*(1.6+b*2.6) + a*2π + sin(t*.7+i*.21+j*.13)*1.4)`.
- Size: `(.42+.58*wave^1.3) * min(1,.5+v*.6) * (keep>0 ? 1 : .8)` times a radius of `.37*step`.
- Cursor: the pointer is eased at 12% per frame. Dots gain `0.7*exp(-d²/(step²*22))` of size near it, capped at 1.05. They are drawn with `arc` and fill.
- Reduced motion: `wave` is fixed at .7.

## 3. FAQ

- Heading `Questions, answered`: 40u, weight 600, tracking -.02em.
- Card: 688u wide, 22u below the heading, 4u by 21u padding, `blur(10u)`, a 1px `rgba(255,190,120,.14)` border, 6u radius and a deep shadow.
- Rows: 17u weight 500 buttons with 17u vertical padding and a 14u chevron that rotates 180° when open. Answers open with a `grid-template-rows: 0fr → 1fr` transition over .4s. They are 15u, line height 1.6, muted colour. Only one answer is open at a time, and the first starts open.
- Questions and answers:
  1. `Which tools does Solace connect to?` — `Solace works with Outlook, Gmail, Slack, Zoom, Figma and Linear, and pulls them into one place so nothing slips between apps.`
  2. `How does Solace decide what is a priority?` — `It weighs deadlines, who is asking and how often a thread comes back, then ranks your day so the one thing that can’t wait sits at the top.`
  3. `Is my data and chat history secure?` — `Everything is encrypted in transit and at rest, nothing is used to train models, and you can export or delete your history at any time.`
  4. `Can I try Solace before I pay?` — `Yes. Every workspace starts with a 14-day trial with every feature switched on, and no card needed.`

## 4. Footer

- Pushed to the bottom with `margin-top:auto`. It is full width, a `1fr auto` grid, with 46u by 64u padding, a gradient from `rgba(40,20,8,.86)` to `rgba(84,40,14,.84)`, `blur(12u)`, a 1px warm border and 6u radius.
- Left: a 38u cream square mark with four dark dots, then the wordmark `Solace` at 25u. Below is the tagline `Your AI co-pilot for the work that matters: priorities, follow-ups and answers across every tool your team already uses.` at 15u, max width 440u. Then four 26u outline icons (LinkedIn, X, Instagram, YouTube), then `© Solace 2026 · All rights reserved` at 14u.
- Right: three 196u columns, with 15u weight 600 headings and 14.5u links:
  - **Product:** Overview, Copilot Chat, Priorities, Integrations, Pricing, Security, Changelog.
  - **Resources:** Docs, Guides, API Reference, Help Center, Status.
  - **Company:** About, Customers, Careers, Contact, Privacy, Terms.

## 5. Phones (820px and below)

The heading is 32px. The FAQ goes full width. The footer becomes one column with 32px by 24px padding and 64px top margin, and the links form two columns.

<script>
// accordion: one answer open at a time
const qs=[...document.querySelectorAll('.q')];
qs.forEach(q=>q.querySelector('button').onclick=()=>{
  const open=q.hasAttribute('data-open');
  qs.forEach(o=>{o.removeAttribute('data-open');o.querySelector('button').setAttribute('aria-expanded','false')});
  if(!open){q.setAttribute('data-open','');q.querySelector('button').setAttribute('aria-expanded','true')}
});

// halftone dot field: a fixed grid whose dots swell and shrink on their own, thin and ragged at the top, dense and pale at the bottom
const cv=document.getElementById('dots'),ctx=cv.getContext('2d');
const calm=matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion:reduce)').matches;
let W=0,H=0,dpr=1,step=0,cols=0,rows=0,seed=[];
let mx=-9999,my=-9999,tmx=-9999,tmy=-9999;
const hash=(i,j)=>{let h=Math.sin(i*127.1+j*311.7)*43758.5453;return h-Math.floor(h)};
function size(){
  dpr=Math.min(devicePixelRatio||1,2);W=cv.clientWidth;H=cv.clientHeight;cv.width=W*dpr;cv.height=H*dpr;ctx.setTransform(dpr,0,0,dpr,0,0);
  step=Math.max(14,Math.min(W/1600,H/940)*20.5);cols=Math.ceil(W/step)+1;rows=Math.ceil(H/step)+1;
  seed=[];for(let j=0;j<rows;j++)for(let i=0;i<cols;i++)seed.push([hash(i,j),hash(i+71,j+13),hash(i+9,j+97)]);
}
addEventListener('resize',size);size();
addEventListener('pointermove',e=>{const r=cv.getBoundingClientRect();tmx=e.clientX-r.left;tmy=e.clientY-r.top});
document.addEventListener('pointerleave',()=>{tmx=tmy=-9999});
// colour runs from a deep orange at the top of the field to pale peach at the bottom
const C0=[226,106,24],C1=[248,150,64],C2=[255,214,170];
const mix=(a,b,t)=>a.map((v,k)=>Math.round(v+(b[k]-v)*t));
function draw(t){
  ctx.clearRect(0,0,W,H);
  mx+=(tmx-mx)*.12;my+=(tmy-my)*.12;
  const top=H*.1,full=H*.36,R=step*.37;
  for(let j=0;j<rows;j++){
    const y=j*step+step*.5;if(y<top-step*2)continue;
    const v=Math.min(1,Math.max(0,(y-top)/(full-top)));         // 0 at the ragged top, 1 lower down
    const col=v<.55?mix(C0,C1,v/.55):mix(C1,C2,(v-.55)/.45*.85+Math.max(0,(y-H*.9)/(H*.1))*.15);
    ctx.fillStyle=`rgb(${col[0]},${col[1]},${col[2]})`;
    for(let i=0;i<cols;i++){
      const x=i*step+step*.5,[a,b,c]=seed[j*cols+i];
      // each dot breathes at its own speed; the top rows are mostly empty with a few survivors
      const wave=calm?.7:.5+.5*Math.sin(t*(1.6+b*2.6)+a*6.283+Math.sin(t*.7+i*.21+j*.13)*1.4);
      const keep=Math.min(1,v*1.6+.12)-(a*.6);
      if(keep<=0&&c>.08)continue;
      let s=(.42+.58*Math.pow(wave,1.3))*Math.min(1,.5+v*.6)*(keep>0?1:.8);
      const dx=x-mx,dy=y-my,d2=dx*dx+dy*dy,hov=Math.exp(-d2/(step*step*22));
      s=Math.min(1.05,s+hov*.7);
      const r=R*s;if(r<.6)continue;
      ctx.beginPath();ctx.arc(x,y,r,0,6.2832);ctx.fill();
    }
  }
}
function loop(ms){draw(ms/1000);requestAnimationFrame(loop)}
requestAnimationFrame(loop);
```

```markdown
# Fernhollow — Night Flower Valley Hero (exact recreation prompt)

Give me a single-file, full-screen hero for a regenerative design studio called **Fernhollow**. It sits on top of an interactive 3D night valley of glowing flowers. A centred cream headline "Grown, not built." in tall condensed type sits over the valley, with a short caption, a round arrow button, a top nav and a sound toggle.

The valley is the 3D flower valley from gladeye.com, used with permission. It is not rebuilt. The page runs the original compiled engine: their webpack runtime and chunks, including three.js r154, the valley scene class, its shaders and its post-processing. It also loads their ten valley assets. The supplied **HTML Code** section contains everything inlined in one file: every script chunk, every asset as a base64 data URI, and both fonts. Use that file as the source of truth. The prompt below describes the interface layer and how the valley is started.

How the valley behaves (all from the original engine):
- **Flowers:** thousands of point-sprite flowers and leaves are scattered over a terrain map. Flowers bloom from small to full size as they approach the camera, and leaves grow in further back.
- **Camera path:** the camera flies along a path baked into `camera-path07.glb`. Wheel or touch moves along it through a virtual scroller (20× touch multiplier). When idle it drifts forward slowly by itself.
- **Mouse:** pushes every point on screen away from the cursor in screen space, with the strongest push close by. Points nearest the cursor glow, and the camera tilts slightly toward the mouse.
- **Effects:** bloom, a split-RGB noise pass, depth fog, light ray sprites, dust particles and a vignette that tightens as you move faster.
- **Hover transition:** `startHoverTransition()` eases the flight to a stop, disperses the flowers outward into floating glowing particles, and muffles the ambient sound through a low-pass filter. `stopHoverTransition()` reverses all of it.
- **Audio:** a looping ambient track through the three.js `AudioListener`. It starts muted and fades in and out when toggled.

---

## 1. Page basics

- Title: `Fernhollow`
- Meta description: `A regenerative design studio. Wander through a night valley of flowers that grows as you move.`
- Fonts: `https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=Antonio:wght@400&family=Manrope:wght@400;500&display=swap`. Antonio is the headline face, and Manrope is used for everything else. The supplied file embeds both.
- Colours: black background, cream `#f5efe2` text, dark text `#151510` on the cream pill.
- Unit: `--u:min(calc(100vw/1600),calc(100vh/900))`, which becomes `1px` at 820px and below.
- `html` and `body` have overflow hidden. `#valley` is fixed full screen and holds `.js-canvas-container`, which the engine mounts its canvas into. The engine's debug panel (`.lil-gui`) is hidden.

## 2. Interface (fixed above the canvas, `pointer-events:none` except links and buttons)

- **Header,** padding 24u top and 44u sides: the wordmark `Fernhollow` at 26u, weight 500. On the right, `Work`, `About`, `Journal` at 14.5u uppercase with .16em tracking and 44u gap, then the cream pill `Let’s talk`, 46u tall with 26u side padding.
- **Hero,** centred horizontally and vertically (`top:50%`, `translateY(-46%)`):
  - `Grown, not built.` in Antonio 400 at 158u, line height .92, tracking -.012em, no wrapping.
  - `Rooted in nature.` / `Built for what’s next.` at 20u, line height 1.3, 48u below.
  - A 58u circle with a 1.5px cream border holding a right arrow, 34u below. It fills cream on hover.
- **Bottom right,** at 44u: `Scroll to wander` at 12.5u uppercase with .16em tracking, a 1px divider 26u tall, then a 28u speaker icon button. It shows a speaker with an X when muted and with waves when playing.
- **Loader:** a black full-screen cover with one pulsing 9u cream dot. It fades out over 1s when the engine reports it has loaded.
- **Interface reveal:** it starts at opacity 0 and fades in over 1.6s the first time the engine reports its intro has finished.

## 3. Starting the original engine

After all chunks have run:

~~~js
self.webpackChunk_N_E.push([[90001],{},function(r){window.__req=r}]);
__req(889);                                   // the valley module
const Valley=window.__GE.et(), audioStore=window.__GE.Y();
let introShown=false;
const valley=new Valley(document.getElementById('valley'),
  ()=>loader.classList.add('gone'),           // onLoaded
  ()=>{ if(!introShown){ introShown=true; ui.classList.add('on') } });  // onIntroDone, called every frame after the intro
audioStore().initAudio();
sound.onclick=()=>{ const s=audioStore(); if(!s.isInitialized) return; const muted=s.toggleMute(); sound.setAttribute('aria-pressed', String(!muted)) };
go.addEventListener('pointerenter',()=>valley.startHoverTransition());
go.addEventListener('pointerleave',()=>valley.stopHoverTransition());
~~~

The page chunk is patched with one line before its `var ew=e=>{` so the module exposes its classes: `window.__GE={et:()=>et,Y:()=>Y};`

In the single-file version, each `"valley/…"` asset path inside the page chunk is replaced by its data URI. The camera path GLB URI must include `name=camera-path.glb`, because the engine picks its loader from the text after the first dot.

## 4. Phones (820px and below)

Header padding is 18px, and the nav links are hidden so only the `Let’s talk` pill shows (40px tall, 12px text). The headline is `clamp(64px,19vw,96px)` and may wrap. The caption is 17px. `Scroll to wander` and the sound button are centred at the bottom, 30px up.
```

```markdown
# Found — The Curiosity Cabinet with a Web-Spinning Spider (exact recreation prompt)

Give me a single-file, full-screen home page for **found**, a personal archive of curious objects called "the curiosity cabinet". The page is flat electric blue with a giant white wordmark `found` in the middle. Collectible cut-out objects float around it: a "Main Character" mug, a frosted glass radio player, a retro laptop in a glass sleeve, a pink book with an iPod, and a "CALL MY LAWYER" t-shirt at the bottom edge.

A photo-real jumping spider lives on the page. It drops in on a silk thread, chases a fly that replaces the mouse cursor, and walks on inverse-kinematics legs cut from one photo. As it moves, it spins real-looking silk threads between the letters and objects: sagging verlet ropes with dew drops, fuzz, iridescence and shadows that fall only on the objects. Click to make it pounce on the fly and wrap it in silk. Press Delete to shake the web off. When it rests, its head crossfades to a cute face that blinks, and later it falls asleep.

All of it runs in one HTML file with a single 2D canvas and no libraries. The live original was a small Preact app, and plain DOM plus vanilla JS is fine. The only external resources are the Inter font, which the supplied file embeds, and three radio streams.

**Source of truth:** the supplied **HTML Code** section is the complete working page. It has all 18 images as base64 data URIs and Inter embedded. Reproduce every value below exactly. When in doubt, copy the behaviour of that file.

---

## 1. Page basics

- Title `Found`. The viewport meta includes `viewport-fit=cover`.
- Font: Inter 400 / 500 / 600 (`https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=Inter:wght@400;500;600&display=swap`). The standalone embeds the latin subset as a woff2 data URI. Stack: `"Inter", system-ui, -apple-system, "Segoe UI", sans-serif`.
- Colours: `--blue: #1129e2` (page), `--ink: #ffffff`, `--ink-70: rgba(255,255,255,0.7)`, `--glass: rgba(255,255,255,0.1)`. `color-scheme: dark`.
- Design frame: a Figma frame 2000 × 1125. `--u: min(calc(100vw / 2000), calc(100dvh / 1125))`.
  - Horizontal positions are in vw (`x / 20 * 1vw`). Vertical positions are in dvh (`y / 11.25 * 1dvh`). Sizes use `--u`, so the composition fills any screen while objects keep their proportions.
- `body` is blue with `overflow: hidden`. `.page` is `100vw × 100dvh`.
- `.frame` holds every element, absolutely positioned, white Inter 400, `user-select: none`.
- Layer order, bottom to top:
  1. `.frame` (all content).
  2. `.web-layer`: one full-size canvas, `pointer-events: none`.
  3. `.over`: a second copy of the big wordmark in which only the letter **o** is visible. This makes the spider crawl *under* the "o" but over the other letters.
- Global cursor: `html, body { cursor: none; touch-action: none; overscroll-behavior: none; user-select: none; -webkit-touch-callout: none }`. Buttons, links and inputs get `cursor: pointer; touch-action: manipulation`.

## 2. Layout (desktop, sizes in u)

- **Mug** (241 × 220 PNG, "Main Character" in handwriting): left `205/20 vw`, top `359/11.25 dvh − 48u`, width 241u.
- **iBook in a glass sleeve** (312 × 377 PNG): right `162/20 vw`, top `323/11.25 dvh`, width 312u.
- **Book and iPod in a glass sleeve** (293 × 322 PNG): right `376/20 vw`, top `689.5/11.25 dvh`, width 293u.
- **T-shirt** (250 × 226 PNG, "CALL MY LAWYER (888) 799-2021" in handwriting): centred, `bottom: 0`, width 250u.
- **Radio player** `.player`:
  - Box: left `max(16px, 7vw)`, top `509/11.25 dvh − 48u`, 291 × 172u. Padding 16u, radius 24u, column gap 12u.

  - **Head:** 40u art thumbnail (radius 12u), title `Support the arts` (18u, weight 600) and sub `date an artist` (12u, 70% white). A 20u heart icon sits on the right.

- **Web anchors:** every element the web can stick to carries `data-web-anchor`: the logo word, each nav link, both nav icons, the big wordmark, the mug, iBook, book, player, headline, tagline and t-shirt. The t-shirt also has `data-stick="bottom"`.

## 3. Responsive

- **Landscape and short** (`min-aspect-ratio:1/1` and `max-height:560px`): `--u: 100dvh/900`. Hide the tagline and mug. Book at right `120/20 vw`.
- **Landscape at 1100px wide or less:** hide the nav links.
- **Portrait** (`max-aspect-ratio:1/1`): `--u: min(100vw/560, 1px)`. Hide the links. Nav top 16px. Then stack from the bottom up:
  - T-shirt 226u at the bottom.
  - Tagline at bottom `226u + 16px`, left and right 16px, wrapping, `max(13px, 26u)`, line height 1.2.
  - Headline at bottom `288u + 32px`, left 16px, 80u.
  - Player at bottom `448u + 56px`, left 16px.

  - iBook at right 3vw, top `50px + 1dvh`, width 165u.
- **Portrait at 700px tall or less:** hide the mug and iBook.
- **Spider scale** `t`:
  - Portrait: `clamp(w/480, .78, 1.1)`.
  - Height under 560: `max(.68, h/620)`.
  - Otherwise: `min(w/1440, h/810)`.
  - Final clamp: .6–1.25.
  - Then spider `size = 1.63·t`, `flySize = max(.75, 1.05·t)`, and the unit `K = size·0.12` px per sprite unit.
```
